Engineering

Naming, folders and stable identities

The manifest is the naming authority for this edition.

On this page
Paths and namesIdentity separationDependencies versus assignmentsRename procedure

Paths and names

Content/Game/Items/DA_Item_CopperOre.uasset is the planned physical path. Its object path is /Game/Game/Items/DA_Item_CopperOre.DA_Item_CopperOre because /Game mounts the Content directory and the project deliberately has a Game subfolder. Do not silently drop the second Game segment in references.

Native public types belong under Source/RPG/Public/<Domain>; implementation files later belong under Source/RPG/Private/<Domain>. The docs list planned header paths only and generate neither .h nor .cpp. Prefixes A/U/F/E/I follow Unreal type conventions; BP_, DA_, WBP_, IA_, IMC_, SPR_, FB_, AS_, ASQ_, ABP_, L_, M_, SM_ describe asset purpose.

Identity separation

Item definition item.copper-ore is not a file path or owned item GUID. CharacterId is not player name. SiteId is not Actor label. EncounterResolutionId is not corpse pointer. RecipeId is not translated recipe title. Use semantic IDs and versioned redirects; never reuse released IDs for different content.

Dependencies versus assignments

Creation dependencies must form a DAG and never require a future phase. Late-binding assignments may point between existing runtime collaborators; each declares its integration phase and reverse user. This avoids creating every shell at00 merely to satisfy a circular blueprint reference. Reopen the consumer at the declared phase and assign the newly ready asset.

Rename procedure

Update the manifest, Content/Source implementation rename/redirect, definition references, UI labels as separate concerns, creation/integration rows and tests. Regenerate all indexes. For released persistent IDs, add a migration/redirect rather than simply renaming. Run unknown-ID and old-record tests before accepting.

Planned game assets are not compiled assets. Values are proposals unless explicitly evidenced. Verification and limitations.
